statement:
The graphs of $y=x^2+5x+6$ and $y=mx-3$, where $m$ is a constant, are plotted on the same set of axes.

Given that the graphs do not meet, what is the complete range of possible values of $m$?
solution:
The graphs do not meet precisely when the simultaneous equations $y=x^2+5x+6$ and $y=mx-3$ have no solutions. Setting them equal,
$$x^2+5x+6=mx-3 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x^2+(5-m)x+9=0.$$

This quadratic has no (real) solutions exactly when its discriminant is negative:
$$(5-m)^2-4\cdot 1\cdot 9 = m^2-10m-11 < 0.$$

Factorising, $(m-11)(m+1)<0$. This quadratic in $m$ has roots $-1$ and $11$, and opens upwards, so it is negative between the roots. Hence
$$-1<m<11,$$
which is **option A**.
hints: The graphs not meeting means the combined quadratic has no real solutions.
Solve the resulting quadratic inequality in m.
